blocks.text: Setting up your book launch database in Notion

A book launch requires tracking dozens of moving parts. You need to monitor review copies, interview requests, and event logistics. Start by creating a primary database for your book projects. Use the /database command to initialize a table view. Name your columns to reflect the lifecycle of a book. Include properties like Author, Publication Date, and Status. This keeps your data structured and searchable.

You can add a status property to track progress. Use tags like Pitching, Scheduled, or Completed. This allows you to create a board view later to see your campaign at a glance. If you need help setting this up, ask Lazur to guide you through the process. Hold your shortcut and say, "Show me how to create a database with status tags."

Your media list is your most valuable asset. Do not keep it in a static spreadsheet. Use a Notion database with a select property for journalist beats. This lets you filter your list when you have a specific book to pitch. You can quickly pull up all journalists who cover historical fiction or tech trends.

blocks.text: Publicist work is reactive. You often need to find information while on a call. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about your screen. You might ask, "Where is the press release draft for the Smith book?" Lazur circles the file or page for you. This saves you from digging through folders during a high-stakes conversation.
Use the fn key to dictate your notes after an author call. Lazur handles the formatting for you. This keeps your records accurate without typing for hours.
blocks.title: Dictate your notes

blocks.text: Many publicists start with too many sub-pages. This makes it hard to find information quickly. Keep your structure flat. Use database filters instead of creating new pages for every contact. If you find yourself clicking through five levels of nested pages, you have gone too deep. Use the ⌘ P shortcut to search your entire workspace instead of relying on the sidebar.

Another common error is failing to use templates. If you create the same media kit structure every time, save it as a database template. Click the arrow next to the blue New button in your database. Select Create a new template. Now you can generate a full campaign structure with one click. This ensures consistency across all your author launches.
Using keyboard shortcuts to save time

Speed is vital when you are managing a launch. Rely on keyboard shortcuts to move through your workspace. Use ⌘ N to create a new page instantly. Use / to open the block menu. If you want to see all available shortcuts, press ⇧ ?. This opens the help menu inside Notion. You can also use ⌘ F to search for text on your current page.

A cluttered workspace leads to missed deadlines. Archive old campaigns regularly. Move completed projects to an Archive database. This keeps your main view focused on active pitches. If you ever need an old contact, you can still find it in the archive. Use a simple status property to filter out archived items from your daily dashboard.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for media list management?
faq.answer: Yes, Notion is excellent for media lists. Use a database with properties for journalist name, outlet, beat, and last contact date. You can filter by beat to find the right contacts for a specific book.

faq.question: How do I speed up my workflow in Notion on Mac?
faq.answer: Use keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ P to search and / to add blocks. Use Lazur by holding ⌥ ⌘ to ask questions about your screen or hold fn to dictate notes directly into your pages.

faq.question: What is the best way to track book launches?
faq.answer: Create a master database for all your books. Use a status property to track the launch phase. Use a board view to see your campaign progress visually.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside the Notion app?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works in any app on your Mac. You can use it to find items on your screen, dictate text, or ask how to perform specific tasks within Notion.
